states.partial: Recognized in a narrower or conditional form
states.no: Not a recognized basis in this form

ccpa.note: An opt-out model. Consent is needed only to sell or share minors' data, to resume after an opt-out, or to join a financial incentive.

appi.note: Consent is needed to go beyond the stated purpose, for sensitive data, and for third-party provision.

nzpa.note: Authorization by the individual is one ground among the principles.

ccpa.note: CCPA uses an opt-out model, not a legal-basis framework.

fadp.note: Listed as an example of an overriding interest, not a standalone basis.

pdpa-ar.note: Processing arising from a contractual relationship.

lpdp-uy.note: Processing necessary for a contractual relationship.

appi.note: No legal-basis framework; contract needs are handled through purpose limits.

nzpa.note: No legal-basis framework; the principles govern collection and use.

dpdp.note: No contract basis. Data you volunteer for a stated purpose comes closest.

ccpa.note: Not framed as a processing basis.

fadp.note: Processing required by law is justified.

appi.note: Cases based on laws are exempt from the consent requirement.

nzpa.note: Collection and use required or authorized by law are permitted.

dpdp.note: Only disclosures the law requires and compliance with court orders.

rows.label: Protection of life or vital interests

ccpa.note: Not framed as a processing basis.

pipa-kr.note: Urgent interests of life, body, or property.

appi.note: Protection of a person's life, body, or property is a consent exemption.

nzpa.note: A serious threat to life or health permits collection and use.

popia.note: Protecting a legitimate interest of the data subject.

dpdp.note: Medical emergencies and threats to life are legitimate uses.

ccpa.note: Not framed as a processing basis.

pipl.note: News reporting and public-opinion oversight in the public interest, within reasonable scope.

fadp.note: An overriding public interest can justify private processing. Federal bodies need a legal basis.

pdpa-ar.note: State databases process for defined public functions.

lpdp-uy.note: Public bodies process for their legal functions.

appi.note: Public-health and child-welfare cooperation is a consent exemption.

nzpa.note: Public-interest grounds appear as specific exceptions.

popia.note: Public-law duty of a public body.

dpdp.note: State functions and public-interest uses are enumerated.

lgpd.note: With a balancing test, set out in ANPD guidance. Not for sensitive data.

ukgdpr.note: With a balancing test. Recognised legitimate interests need none.

fadp.note: Overriding private or public interest is a core justification.

pipa-kr.note: A narrow basis where the controller's interest clearly overrides the person's rights.

appi.note: No legitimate-interests basis; relies on consent and exemptions.

nzpa.note: No named basis; the principles allow reasonable business use.

popia.note: Legitimate interests of the responsible party or a third party.

dpdp.note: No general legitimate-interests basis; only enumerated legitimate uses.

fadp.note: Credit checks are listed as an overriding interest, with conditions. Not a standalone basis.

pdpa-ar.note: Creditworthiness data has a dedicated regime.

lpdp-uy.note: Credit-reporting data has a dedicated regime.

pipa-kr.note: Credit information governed by the separate Credit Information Act.

nzpa.note: Credit reporting governed by a separate Credit Reporting Privacy Code.

gdpr.note: The manifestly-public exemption applies only to special categories. Public data still needs a legal basis.

ccpa.note: Publicly available information is excluded from personal information.

lgpd.note: Manifestly-public data treated with lighter conditions.

pipl.note: Publicly disclosed information within reasonable scope.

ukgdpr.note: The manifestly-public exemption applies only to special categories. Public data still needs a legal basis.

fadp.note: Data made public by the person carries a presumption of no breach.

pdpa-ar.note: Data from unrestricted public sources is exempt from consent.

lpdp-uy.note: Data from public sources is exempt from consent.

pipa-kr.note: Publicly available data may be processed within reasonable expectations.

appi.note: Publicly disclosed data still follows purpose limits.

nzpa.note: Publicly available information is exempt from several principles.

popia.note: Data deliberately made public by the person lifts several conditions.

kdpa.note: Public-source data still subject to fair-processing duties.

dpdp.note: Data the person made public, or must publish by law, falls outside the Act.
